title: Guru Nanak Warns Daulat Khan and Sends Him to Kabul

blocks.text: Daulat Khan presses Guru Nanak to strip sovereignty from the Pathans even if it must pass to another dynasty, but the Guru warns him that once bestowed on the Mughals it would never return to the Pathans. The prophecy does not merely promise a change of rulers; it tells Daulat that he is asking for a transfer he will never be able to undo.

Guru Nanak then turns prediction into instruction. He tells Daulat Khan to go swiftly to Kabul and place the matter before Babur, making clear that the coming upheaval has already entered the field of destiny.

Encouraged by that command, Daulat Khan leaves joyfully in disguise rather than as a grand courtier. The page presents his departure in a fakir's garb as both political secrecy and the first outward sign that the old Pathan order is already cracking.
